Capacity.description:
What a data plane has to give out, in the same units a deployment asks for.

It used to be a single count of deployments, which treated a freemium
instance on 1Gi and an enterprise one on 100Gi as costing the same. The
binding constraint on a cluster running an IAM workload and a Postgres
cluster per deployment is CPU, memory and disk -- not cardinality.

oneOf.description:
Required for `dedicated`, rejected for `shared`. A dedicated data plane
with no owner is one nothing can be placed on; a shared one with an
owner is a contradiction.

cpu_millis.description: CPU in millicores. Defaults with the rest of the sizing.

region.description:
Where to run this. Omitting it uses the control plane's configured
default region; a region that *is* named is never substituted.

last_seen_at.description:
When this data plane's Herald last reported. `None` means it has never
reported since registration, which is not the same failure as having
reported and gone quiet.

oneOf.description: Open to any organisation with room on it.
Reserved to one organisation. Placement for anyone else must not see it.

Dedicated.description: Reserved to one organisation. Placement for anyone else must not see it.

DataPlaneAllocation.description:
What a *data plane* is.

Separate from [`DataPlaneMode`] on purpose. Conflating "what is wanted" with
"what exists" is what would force an `Option<OrganisationId>` next to a
`Dedicated` variant, and with it a runtime check that a dedicated data
plane really has an owner. Here a dedicated one cannot exist without one.

DataPlaneMode.description:
What a *deployment* asks for. Intent, expressed before any data plane has
been chosen -- which is why it carries no organisation: at that point the
organisation comes from the route, not from the mode.

resources.description:
What this deployment costs its data plane, and what its database is
sized to. One value, so the room reserved at placement and the spec
written into the IdentityInstance cannot disagree.

DeploymentResources.description:
What one deployment costs a data plane, and what its database is sized to.

The same value reserves room during placement and is written into the
`IdentityInstance` spec, so the two cannot drift. Before this, placement
counted deployments and Genesis invented the sizing at the other end --
which meant a data plane could accept a deployment it had no disk for.

cpu_millis.description: CPU in millicores, matching Kubernetes' own unit.

recorded.description:
`false` when no data plane carries this id, so a Herald configured with
a stale one learns it instead of reporting into the void.

OrganisationSlug.description: Organisation slug value object (used in URLs)
